events.title: Congress Names the United States
events.description: The Continental Congress formally adopted the name 'United States' for the new nation. It replaced the phrase 'United Colonies' that had been used until then.
events.significance: The change marked a shift from a group of colonies to a declared, independent nation with its own identity.

events.title: The First Computer 'Bug'
events.description: Operators of the Harvard Mark II computer found a moth stuck in a relay. They taped it into the logbook as the first actual case of a bug being found in a computer.
events.significance: The episode helped popularize the term 'debugging', which programmers still use today.

events.title: North Korea Is Founded
events.description: Kim Il-sung declared the establishment of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. This formalized the division of the peninsula under rival governments.
events.significance: The split set the stage for the Korean War and a division that remains one of the world's most enduring geopolitical fault lines.

events.title: Ahmad Shah Massoud Is Assassinated
events.description: Two al-Qaeda operatives killed Ahmad Shah Massoud, a leading Afghan resistance commander. The attack came just two days before the September 11 attacks on the United States.
events.significance: Massoud's death removed a key opponent of the Taliban and is widely seen as a prelude to the September 11 attacks.
